html:
On 4 September 476 Odoacer, a Germanic officer in the Roman army in Italy, removed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna. The date is the usual marker for the end of the Western Roman Empire.

Romulus was a puppet set up by his father Orestes, the army commander. The Germanic soldiers in Italy wanted land, and Orestes refused. They turned to Odoacer, who killed Orestes and spared the boy, sending him to live on a pension in Campania.

Odoacer did not make himself emperor. He sent the imperial regalia to Zeno in Constantinople, saying that one emperor was enough, and ruled Italy as king while keeping the Senate and Roman officials. To people at the time it may not have looked like a great break. In 493 Theoderic and the Ostrogoths, sent by Zeno, killed Odoacer and took Italy.
